title: Patch: the Worker asks again after a failed version check, and a failed retire of the old server no longer fails every request
thread:
**Issue #3771 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #3771: Patch: the Worker asks again after a failed version check, and a failed retire of the old server no longer fails every request
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
When a new server version deploys, the site's front door checks whether the running game server is the old one, and if so restarts it on the new one. Today that check runs once. If the old server is too busy to answer at that moment, the old version keeps running until the server sleeps, which it never does while people play. If the restart itself errors, every request after it fails, and players retrying keep it that way. After this:
- a failed check is tried again a little later;
- the check can't hold a request up indefinitely;
- a failed restart is logged and the request goes through.

## Why
- `apps/edge/src/index.ts:56-57` runs `this.imageChecked ??= this.retireOlderImage(); await this.imageChecked;`, one promise per Durable Object, kept for the object's life.
- A failed `/healthz` fetch returns without retiring (`index.ts:87-94`), so the promise settles as if the check had passed. The old image then serves until the container sleeps (`SLEEP_AFTER`), which live sockets prevent.
- `this.stop('SIGTERM')` and `this.destroy()` (`index.ts:96-101`) are not caught. If either rejects, `imageChecked` stays rejected and every later request through the object throws at line 57.
- The `/healthz` fetch has no timeout, so a hung old server stalls every request queued behind the first.
- `apps/edge/src/index.test.ts:165-172` pins that a failed check still reaches the server. Nothing pins a retry, and no test makes `stop` reject.

## Proposal
- Keep the check's promise only once it succeeds. On a failure, clear it so a later request asks again, no sooner than `IMAGE_CHECK_RETRY_MS` after the last try.
- Bound the fetch with `AbortSignal.timeout(IMAGE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS)`.
- Catch a failed `stop` or `destroy`, log `server.retire_failed`, and go on to start and forward as today.
- Put the constants beside `RETIRE_WAIT_MS` (`index.ts:38`) and add a sentence to `apps/edge/README.md`.
- `/healthz` itself does not change (CLAUDE.md rule 13).

## Where it lands
`apps/edge/src/index.ts`, `apps/edge/src/index.test.ts`, `apps/edge/README.md`.

## Acceptance criteria
The tests use vitest with fake timers:
- [ ] A check that failed is asked again on a request after the retry interval, and an older commit found then is retired.
- [ ] A `stop` that rejects once leaves that request and the next one answered.
- [ ] A `/healthz` that never answers lets the request through after the timeout.
- [ ] A check that succeeded is not repeated.
- [ ] `pnpm exec vitest run --project edge` is green.

## Size and risks
- Small to medium: 3 files and about 80 lines plus tests.
- Open issue #3618 also edits `index.ts`, so the two may conflict.
- How often the platform rejects these calls is unknown. This is insurance against an outage, not a fix for one already seen.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

## Plan

_Written by `claude-6` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43233078250)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`Server.fetch` in the Worker (`apps/edge/src/index.ts`) keeps the image check's result only once the check has succeeded. After a failure it asks again on a later request, no sooner than `IMAGE_CHECK_RETRY_MS` after the last attempt. The `/healthz` fetch is bounded by `AbortSignal.timeout(IMAGE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS)`. A rejected `stop` or `destroy` is caught and logged as `server.retire_failed`, and the request goes on to start and forward. `/healthz` itself does not change (CLAUDE.md rule 13).

## Files to touch

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `apps/edge/src/index.ts` | `change`: add `IMAGE_CHECK_RETRY_MS` and `IMAGE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` beside `RETIRE_WAIT_MS`. Replace the `imageChecked` promise with three fields and `ensureImageChecked()`. `retireOlderImage()` now returns `Promise<boolean>`, never rejects, and times out its fetch. |
| `apps/edge/src/index.test.ts` | `change`: update the `{}` expectation in the `/healthz` test, and add tests for retry, timeout, rejected `stop` and `destroy`, and no repeat after success. |
| `apps/edge/README.md` | `change`: one sentence in the "A deploy reaches the running server" bullet (line 36-40). |

Do not touch `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `.claude/`, `spec/`, `crates/`, `apps/web`, `routing.ts` or `wrangler.jsonc`. No spec ruling and no patch fragment are needed, because there is no rules or catalog change. Open issue #3618 also edits `index.ts`, so keep the diff to the lines below to limit conflicts.

## Steps

1. In `apps/edge/src/index.ts`, after `RETIRE_POLL_MS` (line 39), add these exported constants, each with a one-line doc comment:
   ```ts
   /** The least time between two image checks that failed: a request inside it skips the check. */
   export const IMAGE_CHECK_RETRY_MS = 10_000;
   /** How long the `/healthz` fetch of the image check may take before it counts as failed. */
   export const IMAGE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000;
   ```
2. Replace the field at lines 52-53 with:
   ```ts
   /** True once a check has completed, a deploy restarts this object, so the first request after one checks the running image. */
   private imageVerified = false;
   /** The check in flight, shared by the requests that arrive while it runs. */
   private imageCheck: Promise<void> | undefined;
   /** When the last check began (`Date.now()`); a failed one is not retried before `IMAGE_CHECK_RETRY_MS` has passed. */
   private imageCheckedAt: number | undefined;
   ```
3. In `fetch` (lines 55-60), replace lines 56-57 with `await this.ensureImageChecked();`. Leave the `awaitStart` and `super.fetch` lines as they are.
4. Add the private method `ensureImageChecked(): Promise<void>`:
   - If `this.imageVerified`, return.
   - If `this.imageCheck` is undefined:
     - If `this.imageCheckedAt !== undefined && Date.now() - this.imageCheckedAt < IMAGE_CHECK_RETRY_MS`, return. The request goes on without a check.
     - Otherwise set `this.imageCheckedAt = Date.now()`.
     - Then set `this.imageCheck = this.retireOlderImage().then((done) => { this.imageVerified = done; this.imageCheck = undefined; })`.
   - Finally `await this.imageCheck`.
   - `retireOlderImage` never rejects (step 5), so the `.then` always runs and `imageCheck` is always cleared.
5. Rewrite `retireOlderImage(): Promise<boolean>`. `true` means the check is settled: the container was not running, the commit matched, or the old server was retired. `false` means ask again later. Keep the doc comment and add a sentence on the retry.
   - `if (!this.ctx.container?.running) return true;`
   - In the existing `try`, change the fetch to `this.containerFetch(`http://container${HEALTH_PATH}`, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(IMAGE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS) }, SERVER_PORT)`. Keep the `catch` that logs `console.warn("server.image_check_failed", error)`, but `return false`. Update its comment to say that the request goes on and a later one asks again.
   - `if (running === (this.env.DEPLOYED_COMMIT ?? null)) return true;`
   - Wrap the retire block in a new `try`: `await this.stop("SIGTERM")`, then the `deadline` loop, then `if (this.ctx.container.running) await this.destroy();`, then `return true`.
   - Its `catch (error)` runs `console.warn("server.retire_failed", error); return false;`.
   - Keep `RETIRE_WAIT_MS` and `RETIRE_POLL_MS` as they are.
   - After a failed retire the request goes on to `awaitStart`, which starts a container if it is down and otherwise forwards to the old server. The next request after the interval tries again.
6. In `apps/edge/README.md`, append to the "A deploy reaches the running server" bullet (after "(SPEC §9.5)."):
   > A check that fails (the old server does not answer `/healthz` within `IMAGE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS`, or the stop errors) is logged (`server.image_check_failed`, `server.retire_failed`), the request goes through, and a later request asks again, no sooner than `IMAGE_CHECK_RETRY_MS` after the last try.
7. In `apps/edge/src/index.test.ts`, update the import to add `IMAGE_CHECK_RETRY_MS` and `IMAGE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS`. In the test at line 137, change the expected second argument from `{}` to `{ signal: expect.any(AbortSignal) as unknown }`. Then add the tests below.

## Tests

All new tests go inside `describe("the image check on the first request")` (rename it to `"the image check"` if you like). `beforeEach` already calls `resetLibrary()`. Define two helpers in that describe:
- `const OLDER = () => new Response(null, { headers: { "x-deployed-commit": "older" } });`
- `warn = vi.spyOn(console, "warn").mockImplementation(() => undefined)`, as the existing tests do.

Use `vi.useFakeTimers()` in a `try`/`finally { vi.useRealTimers(); }`, as the test at line 188 does. Build one `Server` per test with `serverWithCtx({ container }, { DEPLOYED_COMMIT: COMMIT })` and a mutable `container = { running: true }`. Call `.fetch(request())` on that same instance several times.

1. `"asks again after the retry interval when the check failed, and retires an older commit then"`:
   - `containerFetch` is `mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error("no answer"))`, then `mockResolvedValue(OLDER())`.
   - `stop` sets `container.running = false`.
   - First request: answered, `containerFetch` called once, `stop` not called.
   - Second request at once, with no timer advance: `containerFetch` still called once. This pins the retry floor.
   - `vi.advanceTimersByTime(IMAGE_CHECK_RETRY_MS)`, then a third request: `containerFetch` called twice and `stop` called with `"SIGTERM"`.
2. `"leaves that request and the next one answered when stop rejects once"`:
   - `containerFetch` returns `OLDER()`, `stop` is `mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error("refused"))`, and `container.running` stays true.
   - The first request resolves to `LISTENING`, `warn` was called with `"server.retire_failed", expect.any(Error)`, and `destroy` was not called.
   - Advance by `IMAGE_CHECK_RETRY_MS`. For the second `stop` call, set `container.running = false` and resolve.
   - The second request resolves to `LISTENING` and `stop` has been called twice.
3. `"logs a destroy that rejects and still answers"`:
   - `containerFetch` returns `OLDER()` and `container.running` stays true.
   - `destroy` is `mockRejectedValueOnce`.
   - Start `fetching = server.fetch(request())`, `await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(30_000)`, then `expect(await fetching).toBe(LISTENING)`.
   - Assert `warn` was called with `"server.retire_failed"`.
4. `"lets the request through when /healthz never answers, once the timeout passes"`:
   - Under fake timers a native `AbortSignal.timeout` would not fire, so control the signal. Create `const controller = new AbortController()` and `const timeout = vi.spyOn(AbortSignal, "timeout").mockReturnValue(controller.signal)`.
   - `containerFetch.mockImplementation((_url, init) => new Promise((_, reject) => { (init as RequestInit).signal!.addEventListener("abort", () => reject(new Error("timed out"))); }))`.
   - Start `fetching`, and `await Promise.resolve()` so it reaches the fetch.
   - Assert `timeout` was called with `IMAGE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` and that `fetching` has not settled.
   - Call `controller.abort()`, then `expect(await fetching).toBe(LISTENING)`.
   - Assert `warn` was called with `"server.image_check_failed"`.
   - Call `timeout.mockRestore()` in `finally`.
5. `"does not repeat a check that succeeded"`:
   - Matching commit. Make two requests with an `IMAGE_CHECK_RETRY_MS * 3` timer advance between them.
   - `containerFetch` is called once.
6. `"does not repeat a check that retired the old server"` (optional). It is like test 1, but the check succeeds on the first try. After the advance, a second request must leave `containerFetch` at one call.

The existing tests at lines 165-172 (failed check still reaches the server) and 174-206 must pass unchanged, apart from the step 7 edit.

Commands:
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project edge`
- `pnpm exec eslint apps/edge`
- `pnpm --dir apps/edge exec tsc --noEmit -p .` (or `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` if edge has no typecheck script, since `apps/edge/tsconfig.json` exists). This confirms that `containerFetch`'s second argument accepts `{ signal }`.

## Done when

- [ ] A failed check is retried on a request after `IMAGE_CHECK_RETRY_MS`, and an older commit found then is retired.
- [ ] The `/healthz` fetch carries `AbortSignal.timeout(IMAGE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS)`, and a hung check lets the request through.
- [ ] A rejected `stop` or `destroy` logs `server.retire_failed`, and the request and the next one are answered.
- [ ] A check that succeeded is not repeated.
- [ ] The README sentence is added, and the two constants sit beside `RETIRE_WAIT_MS`.
- [ ] `pnpm exec vitest run --project edge`, eslint and the typecheck are green.
- [ ] The harness checks pass (`cargo fmt --check` etc.). No Rust or spec files are touched.

## Risks

- **Check rejecting.** If `retireOlderImage` ever rejected, `imageCheck` would never clear and every request would throw, which is the bug being fixed. Keep every `await` inside it within a `try`. The outer `.then` does not clear on rejection.
- **Concurrent requests.** Concurrent requests share the in-flight `imageCheck`, and a request inside the retry window skips the check without waiting.
- **Timeout in tests.** A native `AbortSignal.timeout` timer is not faked by vitest, so test 4 stubs `AbortSignal.timeout`. Restore it afterwards so other tests are not affected.
- **Rate limit on `/healthz`.** The check is rate-limited by `IMAGE_CHECK_RETRY_MS`, so a down old server is not asked on every request.
- **Conflict with #3618.** Keep edits to `index.ts` to the regions named above.

## Open questions

- The values `IMAGE_CHECK_RETRY_MS = 10_000` and `IMAGE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000` are my picks, because the issue names the constants but not their values. 5 s is well under `START_WAIT_MS`, and 10 s keeps a retry from being hit on every request. A person can change them in review.
- Design decision: a failed `stop` or `destroy` also counts as "not checked", so it is retried later, rather than being treated as done. I rejected treating it as done because the old image would then keep serving, which is the problem the issue describes.
````
